 JUDGMENT The Police Sub Inspector of Madivala P.S has submitted the Charge Sheet against the accused for the offences punishable Under Sec. 285 and 420 of IPC. 
2. The brief facts of the Prosecution case are as follows:
That on 31/1/2013 at about 3-00 p.m. the accused with an intention to cheat the government/public by selling them in black market for higher price and without any precautionary measures had stored the gas cylinders at Anand Reddy Building No.163/101, 6th Cross, Maruthi Layout, Devarachikkanahalli, Maruthilayout,
Bengalore. Thereby the accused has committed the offences punishable U/Sec.285 and 420 of IPC. 
3. On the basis of the Statement of CW-1, the Madivala Police have registered a case under Crime No.84/2013 for the offences punishable U/s 420 and 285 of IPC against the accused and submitted the FIR before the court. Thereafter investigating officer visited the spot and drawn the spot mahazar and recorded the statement of witnesses on completion of the investigation, the Charge Sheet has been filed against the accused for the offences punishable U/Sec. 285 and 420 of IPC. On the receipt of the police report, this court has taken cognizance for the said offences. 
4. On the appearance of the accused, the accused was enlarged on bail. The copies of prosecution papers were furnished to the accused as contemplated U/Sec.207 of Cr.P.C. After hearing both the parties, the charge was framed against the accused for the offences punishable U/Sec.285 and 420 of IPC and Sec.7(1)(A)(I) of Essential Commodities Act 1955 and Sec.3 and 7 of Liquified Petroleum Gas supply and Distributin Order C V Deepak Pi vs Ranganath on 4 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106956774/
2 -2000 and read over to him. Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. Hence, the matter was posted for evidence. 
5. In order to bring home the guilt of the accused, the prosecution has got examined four witnesses as PW-1 to 4, out of the total charge sheet witnesses as CW-1 to 9 and got marked three documents as Ex.P1 to P3. Learned A.P.P given up the examination of C.W.2, 3 and 7. Learned Sr.APP prayed for issuance of summons to C.W.5 and 6 inspite of giving sufficient opportunities to I.O to execute summons, NBW and proclamation the witnesses have not been secured. Hence, the evidence of C.W.5 and 6 is dropped by rejecting the prayer of the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor. After closure of prosecution evidence the accused is examined U/s 313(1)(b) Cr.P.C and each and every circumstance found in the evidence is read over separately to the accused. The accused denied all such incriminating circumstances as false. Accused did not choose to explain anything during his examination. Accused did not choose to adduce defence evidence and during the course of cross examination PW3 got confronted and got marked document as Ex.D.1. 
6. I have heard the arguments addressed by the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor and learned advocate for the accused. 
7. On going through the facts and circumstances of the prosecution case, the following points would arise for my consideration :
POINTS 1. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on 31/1/2013 at about 3-00 p.m. at Devarachikkanahalli, 6th Cross, Maruthi Layout, Anand Reddy Building No.163/101 the accused with an intention to make wrongful gain and to cheat the public possessed domestic and commercial gas cylinders of various companies and thereby the accused has committed the offence punishable U/s 420 of IPC ?
2. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on the above said date, time and place the accused with an intention to make wrongful gain possessed domestic and commercial gas cylinders of various companies and accused would refill small gas cylinders without adhering to safety measures and thereby the accused has committed the offence punishable U/s 285 of the IPC?
3. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on the above said date, time and place the accused was refilling small gas cylinders without adhering to safety measures would sell the refilled small gas cylinders for a higher price and cheated the public and Government and thereby the accused has committed the offences punishable Sec.7(1)(A)(I) of Essential Commodities Act 1955 and Sec.3 and 7 of Liquified Petroleum Gas supply and Distribution Order -2000?"
4. What Order ?

 Point No.1 to 3 : In the Negative.

 REA S ON S  9. Points No.1 to 3 :- As these points are interlinked with each other and also similar evidence is led on all these points, I have taken all these points together for common discussion in order to avoid repetition of facts and discussion.
10. It is the case of the prosecution that the accused with an intention to cheat the Government/Public and without following any precautionary measures had stored gas cylinders at Ananda Reddy building, at 6th cross, Bommanahalli, Maruthi Layout, Bengaluru. The I.O seized both filled and empty gas cylinders totalling upto 54 cylinders. Thereby the accused has committed the offences punishable U/Sec.285 and 420 of IPC.
11. In order to prove its case, the prosecution has got examined the informant of crime/C.W.1- C.V.Deepak as P.W.1, C.W.4-Paramesh as P.W.2 and C.W.9-Paul PriyaKumar as P.W.3 and C.W.8/Srinivas G.T is examined as P.W.4. 
Out of the documents marked for the prosecution Ex.P1 is the complaint, Ex.P.2 is the mahazar and Ex.P.3 is the FIR . During the course of cross examination of PW3 he got confronted and got marked document as ExD1. Ex.D1 is the xerox copy of the bill pertaining to D.K.Agency.
12. In support of the case of prosecution informant of crime/C.W1 is examined as P.W1. 
P.W.1-Sri.C.V.Deepak- Dy.S.P. STF, Bengaluru, in his evidence deposed that on 31.01.2013 he received credible information that the accsued Ranganatha without valid license was refilling gas from domestic gas cylinders to commercial gas cylinders and was selling them for a higher prices to the public and was making illegal gain and he conducted raid at building No. 163/101, 6 th cross,
Kasturba road, Devarachikkanahalli, Maruthi Layout along with C.W.2 to 4(police staff) and found the accused in possession of 24 cylinders of 14.2kgs each and 14 empty cyinders and 06 cylinders of 19 kgs each in the godown and he seized the same and drew mahazar which is at Ex.P.2 in the presence of panchas and prepared the complaint which is at Ex.P.1.
This witness was cross examined by the Learned counsel for accused and in the cross examination he deposed that he has not mentioned about receiving credible information and conducting raid in the Station House Diary. He admitted that the owner of building No.163/101 situated at Devarachikkanahalli, 6 th cross is Ananda Reddy and he has not taken any documents pertaining to the rent or lease agreement as to accused was holding a godown in the building of Ananda Reddy. 
Further he admitted that he had no trouble to take the photographs of the office and godown. He further deposed that police staff by name Paramesh prepared Ex.P.2 as per his direction. He denied C V Deepak Pi vs Ranganath on 4 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106956774/
4 the suggestion that he did not visit the spot and draw spot mahazar. He deposed that he does not know that Bengaluru Gas Agency was the owner of the said Godown. He deposed that he has not given the information to the Food and Civil Supplies Department about illegally possessing gas cylinders. He denied the suggestion that he prepared Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2. He denied the suggestion that the accused is working as delivery person at Bengaluru Gas Agency and he has not committed the alleged offences. He denied the suggestion that there in no relation between the accused and Anand Reddy building. He denied the suggestion that he has filed false complaint against the accused for statistical purpose. 
13. C.W.4/P.W.2- Paramesh- ASI- in his evidence deposed that on 31.01.2013 at 5.00 P.M, he along with C.W.1, 3 and 4 along with panchas i.e C.W.5 and 6 conducted raid at building No. 163/101, 6th cross, Kasturba road, Devarachikkanahalli, Maruthi Layout and found the accused in possession of of 24 cylinders of 14.2kgs each and 14 empty cylinders and 06 cylinders of 19 kgs each in the godown and C.W.1 seized the same and drew mahazar as per Ex.P.2 in the presence of panchas. 
This witness was cross examined by the Learned counsel for accused and in the cross examination he deposed that he went to the spot at about 3.40 P.M and C.W1 secured the panchas and C.W.1 conducted enquiry from 3.30P.M to 5.30P.M. He denied the suggestion that Ex.P.2 was prepared at the police station and panchas signed on the mahazar at the police station. He denied the suggestion that he is seeing the accused for the first time at the court and he deposed that he has not mentioned about the identity of the accused in his statement. 
14. C.W.9/P.W3- Paul PriyaKumar-Police Inspector, in his evidence deposed that after completing investigation he filed the charge sheet against the accused. 
During cross examination of this witness a xerox copy of the bill pertaining to D.K.Agency was confronted and Ex.D.1 was got marked. He admitted that the date in the bill is mentioned as 23.02.2013 and alleged incident took place on 31.01.2013. He admitted the suggestion that the Ex.D1 is a record 23 days afer the incident. He denied the suggestion that accused has not committed any offence as alleged and he is deposing false to help the C.W.1.
15. C.W.8/P.W.4-Srinivas.G.T- Police Inspector, in his evidence deposed that on 31.01.2013 the C.W.1 appeared before him and lodged written complaint as per Ex.P.1 and registered the complaint and sent FIR to the court and he produced 54 cylinders and the accused at the police station and subjected the gas cylinders to Property form No.16/13. He further deposed that he produced the accused before court. 
Learned counsel for accused cross examined P.W.4 at length and P.W.4 denied the suggestion that on 31.01.2013 C.W.1 did not come to the police station and lodge a written complaint and did not produce 54 cylinders. He deposed that at the time of releasing the gas cylinders to the owner/petitioner, he said that he does not know the accused person. He denied the suggestion that the accused is working as delivery boy at Bengaluru Gas Agency and he deposed that he does not know whether customers have recieved the gas cylinders as per the xerox bills produced in this case. 
He denied the suggestion that he is deposing false with a view to help C.W.1 C V Deepak Pi vs Ranganath on 4 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106956774/
5 16. The prosecution failed to secure other witnesses inspite of giving sufficient opportunities. During course of trial, the accused taken up defence of total denial of the case of the prosecution. 
17. In the light of above evidence, the learned APP argued that although most of the witnesses have not supported the case of prosecution, yet there is evidence to believe that the act committed by the accused is nothing but cheating there is sufficient material on record to convict the accused. 
Therefore, he prayed to convict the accused. 
The learned advocate for accused argued that, the material witnesses to the case of prosecution have not supported the case. There is nothing on record to believe that accused has committed offences punishable Under Secs.420, 285 of Indian Penal Code and Sec.7(1)(A)(I) of Essential Commodities Act 1955 and Sec.3 and 7 of Liquified Petroleum Gas supply and Distribution Order -2000. The prosecution has failed to prove the offence beyond reasonable doubt. Therefore, he prayed to acquit the accused. 
18. I have carefully gone through the charges levelled against the accused and also the evidence relied by the prosecution. On behalf of the accused it is argued that the accused was working as gas cylinder supply man/delivery boy. Further it is argued that there is no satisfactory evidence to establish the guilt of the accused and accordingly it is prayed to acquit the accused. 
19. In the decision reported in (2017) 11 SCC 195- Yogesh Singh Vs Mahabeer Singh and others ..At para 15 Hon'ble Supreme Court observed as under:
"15. It is a cardinal principle of criminal jurisprudence that the guilt of the accused must be proved beyond all reasonable doubts. However, the burden on the prosecution is only to establish its case beyond all reasonable doubt and not all doubts". 
Here, it is worthwhile to reproduce the observations made by Venkatachaliah, ., in State of U.P. Vs.
Krishna Gopal and Anr., (1988) 4 SCC 302:
"25. ... Doubts would be called reasonable if they are free from a zest for abstract speculation. Law cannot afford any favorite other than truth. To constitute reasonable doubt, it must be free from an overemotional response. Doubts must be actual and substantial doubts as to the guilt of the accused person arising from the evidence, or from the lack of it, as opposed to mere vague apprehensions. A reasonable doubt is not an imaginary, trivial or a merely possible doubt; but a fair doubt based upon reason and common sense. It must grow out of the evidence in the case". 
Keeping the requirement of the above said provisions of law and law laid down in the above said decision in my mind I have carefully examined the evidence placed on record.

6 20. This court noticed that P.W.1 to 4 who are examined in support of the case of prosecution are all interested witnesses. The evidence of these witnesses is to be scrutinized cautiously. No independent eye witness has been cited in the charge sheet. Further more the prosecution has not examined any independent witnesses in support of its case. Therefore, there is no independent corroboration to the case of prosecution. There is no information as to who is the owner of the godown where the accused illegally possessed/stored 54 gas cylinders. The C.W.1 has not furnished any photo or documentary evidence to show that the accused was at the alleged place of incident when he conducted raid. PW1 has not recorded the statement of adjoining building. 
21. It is the burden of the prosecution to show that they have seized the alleged goods from the possession of the accused in the presence of pancha witnesses under seizure mahazar. To prove the facts of the evidence the complainant and also the pancha witnesses are very essential. 
22. On perusal of the evidence adduced by the prosecution in support of their case, as already stated above the Seizure Mahazar Witness has not been examined, so it clearly reveals that the Mahazar is not proved beyond all reasonable doubt. 
23. There are no independent witnesses to the case of prosecution. Although the place of incident is a town, no independent witnesses are cited as the witnesses. The evidence of PW-1 to 4 is not corroborative to each other. 
24. In the absence of corroborative evidence, the contents of exhibits are also not sufficient to prove the case of prosecution beyond reasonable doubts. Further there is no corroboration in the evidence of the official witnesses also. 
25. Looking to the weak type of evidence, there are two possibilities, one pointing towards the guilt of accused and another pointing towards the innocence of the accused. Therefore, looking to the entire material on record, I am of the considered opinion that the prosecution has failed to prove beyond reasonable doubt that the accused has committed the alleged offences. 
26. On careful appreciation of evidence led on behalf of prosecution, it reveals that, none of the witnesses have spoken to with regard to essential ingredients constituting the offence of refilling small cylinders and regarding the offence U/s 285 of IPC. No material has been seized by the IO to show that the accused was selling the refilled small gas cylinders or refilling gas to small cylinders as alleged in the complaint. Hence, on careful and meticulous appreciation of evidence and considering the totality of circumstances, the prosecution has failed to prove beyond all reasonable doubt that,
the charges leveled against the accused. Further in this particular case, the defence of the accused is that, the police have falsely implicated the accused in order to show statistic to the state. When the prosecution has not proved the seizure mahazar with independent evidence, the evidence of other officials is formal in nature. In the absence of corroborative evidence, only on the basis of the official witnesses, this court cannot come to the conclusion that the accused committed the offence as alleged by the Prosecution. When the Prosecution has not proved its case, beyond all reasonable doubt, it creates doubt in the mind of this court. Hence, the accused is entitled to get benefit of doubt and he is entitled for acquittal. Hence, considering the over all circumstances of the case I C V Deepak Pi vs Ranganath on 4 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106956774/
7 answer point Nos.1 to 3 in the Negative".
27. Point No.4: - In view of Negative findings on the above points, accused is entitled for acquittal on doubt benefit. Hence, I proceed to pass the following:
ORD ER Acting U/Sec.248(1) of Cr.P.C. accused is acquitted of the offences punishable U/Sec.285 and 420 of IPC and Sec.7(1)(A)(I) of Essential Commodities Act 1955 and Sec.3 and 7 of Liquified Petroleum Gas supply and Distribution Order -2000. 
Bail bonds of the accused and Surety bonds shall stand canceled. 
The interim custody of the property mentioned in P.F. No. 16/2013 is made absolute. 
The bail bond executed U/Sec. 437(A) of Cr.P.C shall be continued.
